query: The Broom That Pulls Left Your loft broom pulls left, always has. With the jar's wind behind it, it would pull you into the lake. The broom-maker in the village can true it, for a price. Pay to have it trued The broom-maker sights along it, tuts, and spends an afternoon on it. It flies straight for the first time in living memory. You miss the pull, a little. Learn to fly it crooked You learn to lean right all the time. Your back complains, and the broom keeps pulling left out of habit.
